questions.question_text_en: From the magnitude of the equilibrium constant, Keq one can deduce that

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: large Keq value indicates that the reaction reaches equilibrium with very little reactants remaining.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Small Keq values indicate the reaction yields very higher amounts of products near equilibrium.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Keq will be larger when we have higher amounts of reactants over products.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Intermediate Keq value indicates that the reaction does proceed in the forward direction.

explanation.solution_text_en:
A large equilibrium constant means products are strongly favored, so only a relatively small amount of reactant 
remains at equilibrium.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 11 Chemistry — Unit 5: Chemical Equilibrium

questions.question_text_en:
The statement 'If a system at equilibrium is subjected to a stress, the system will readjust itself to reduce the effects of the 
stress' is known as

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Avogadro's principle.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Faradays law.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Le-Chatelier's principle.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Boyle's law.

explanation.solution_text_en:
Le Chatelier’s principle states that an equilibrium system shifts in the direction that counteracts an imposed change 
in concentration, pressure, or temperature.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 11 Chemistry — Unit 5: Chemical Equilibrium

questions.question_text_en: The law of mass action states that

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: The Keq expression is the ratio of the concentrations of reactants to the products raised to their coefficients.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en:
The rate of a reaction is directly proportional to the product of the concentration of reactants raised to the power of their 
respective coefficients in the balanced equation.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: For a reaction at equilibrium, the reaction quotient, Q is always less than the equilibrium constant, Keq.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: A chemical equilibrium is attained only when the reaction is started with reactants.

explanation.solution_text_en:
The law of mass action relates reaction rate to the product of reactant concentrations, each raised to the appropriate 
stoichiometric power.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 11 Chemistry — Unit 5: Chemical Equilibrium

questions.question_text_en:
For the reaction between gaseous NO and O₂ to for NO₂ (g), what will be the equilibrium constant expression, 2NO(g) + O₂ 
(g)↔ 2NO₂ (g)

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: K p =(P NO2)/(P NO)(P O2)

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: K c =(NO₂)² / (NO)² (O₂)

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: K p =(P NO2)² (P O2) / (P NO2)

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: K p =(P NO2)² /(NO)² (O₂)

explanation.solution_text_en: For 2NO + O₂ ⇌ 2NO₂, the concentration expression is Kc = [NO₂]² / ([NO]²[O₂]), which corresponds to option B.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 11 Chemistry — Unit 5: Chemical Equilibrium

questions.question_text_en:
The equilibrium constant K p for the reaction 2SO₂ (g) ⇌ 2SO₃ (g) + O₂ (g) is 3.8 × 10⁻³ K p at 227 °C. What is the value of K 
c for the reaction at the same temperature?
questions.review_note: Defective calculation item: the equation/options do not produce a listed Kc value.

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: 4.6 × 10⁻⁴ mol m⁻³

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: 1.8 × 10⁻³ mol m⁻³

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: 2.3 × 10⁻⁴ mol m⁻³

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: 9.1 × 10⁻⁴ mol m⁻³

explanation.solution_text_en:
As printed, Δn(gas) = 3 − 2 = +1, so Kp = Kc(RT). At 500 K, Kc ≈ 9.3 × 10⁻⁵, which is not among the choices. The 
item is defective as supplied.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 11 Chemistry — Unit 5: Chemical Equilibrium

questions.question_text_en:
In the Galvanic cell given in the diagram below Identify the component parts correctly labelled for the letters a, b, c, d and 
choose the correct one among the following a, b, c, and d, respectively

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Copper anode; Zinc cathode; voltmeter; salt bridge

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Zinc anode; Copper cathode; salt bridge; voltmeter

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Copper anode; Zinc anode; CuSO₄(aq); voltmeter

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Zinc anode; Copper cathode; ZnSO₄(aq); salt bridge

explanation.solution_text_en:
In a Daniell-type Zn/Cu galvanic cell, Zn is the anode where oxidation occurs, Cu is the cathode where reduction 
occurs, the salt bridge maintains charge balance, and the voltmeter measures cell potential. The same-exam scan identifies this 
sequence as option B.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 12 Chemistry — Unit 2: Electrochemistry

questions.question_text_en: The conversion of nitrogen gas into useful nitrogen compounds is known as

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Photosynthesis

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Respiration

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Oxidation

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Fixation

explanation.solution_text_en:
Nitrogen fixation converts atmospheric N₂ into chemically usable nitrogen compounds such as ammonia or related 
species.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 12 Chemistry — Unit 3: Industrial Chemistry (nitrogen/ammonia context)

questions.question_text_en: CO₂ is released into the atmosphere by one of the following processes

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Animals eat plants and release CO₂ by photosynthesis

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Plants consume atmospheric carbon dioxide during photosynthesis

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Utilization of electrical energy as energy sources

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Natural fires and volcanoes release CO₂ into the air

explanation.solution_text_en: Natural fires and volcanic activity release CO₂. Photosynthesis instead removes CO₂ from the atmosphere.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 12 Chemistry — Unit 5: Introduction to Environmental Chemistry

questions.question_text_en: One of the following is NOT a common application of silicon

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: in the control of the frequency of television transmissions

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: in the construction of transistors and microprocessors

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: in coating iron to prevent it from rusting

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: in the production of polish body parts cars

explanation.solution_text_en:
Silicon is central to semiconductors and electronics, but coating iron to prevent rusting is not a common application 
of elemental silicon.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 10 Chemistry — Unit 5: Metals and Nonmetals

questions.question_text_en: One of the following is NOT among the chemical properties of silicon

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Silica is resistant to attack by all acids except HF, which it reacts to give SiF₄ and H₂ O₂

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Silicon reacts with CH₃ Cl at 300 °C in the Cu as a catalyst by further reactions with H₂ O yields the polymer [(CH₃)₂ SiO₂ ] n

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Silicon occurs as silica (SiO₂) and silicate compounds containing the silicate ion (SiO₄⁴⁻)

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Silica dissolves in hot molten Na₂ CO₃ to give Na₄ SiO₄ and CO₂

explanation.solution_text_en:
“Silicon occurs as silica and silicates” describes occurrence, not a chemical property or reaction of silicon; therefore 
C is the NOT item.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 10 Chemistry — Unit 5: Metals and Nonmetals

questions.question_text_en:
The branch of chemistry that is involved in separation, identifying and determining the relative amounts of components in a 
sample of material is known as

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: analytical chemistry

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: biochemistry

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: inorganic chemistry

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: physical chemistry

explanation.solution_text_en: Analytical chemistry focuses on separating, identifying, and quantitatively determining components of a sample.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 9 Chemistry — Unit 1: Chemistry and Its Importance

questions.question_text_en: Significant figures are figures with

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: measured values with the highest accuracy

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: measured values with the highest precision

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: exactly known digits with the last digit uncertain

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: measured values with the highest uncertainty

explanation.solution_text_en: All certain digits plus the first uncertain estimated digit are counted as significant figures.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 9 Chemistry — Unit 2: Measurements and Scientific Methods

questions.question_text_en:
For the determination of the density of a new ceramic, a student measured the mass of a piece on an analytical balance and 
obtained 3.8056 gram and its volume 2.5 mL by displacement of water in a graduated cylinder. The correct reported density 
of the ceramic should be

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: 3.5 g/mL

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: 1.5 g/mL

explanation.solution_text_en: Density = 3.8056 g / 2.5 mL = 1.52224 g/mL. The volume has two significant figures, so the result is 1.5 g/mL.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 9 Chemistry — Unit 2: Measurements and Scientific Methods

questions.question_text_en: The scientific method is

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: a method of arriving at an organized body of knowledge based on reproducible experiments and observations

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: a collection of scientific guesses and hypotheses by seeking patterns in the observations

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: the result of fortunate, accidental discovery in the development of science

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: the sum total of unique guidelines for the practice of science in the world

explanation.solution_text_en: The scientific method builds organized, testable knowledge through reproducible observation and experiment.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 9 Chemistry — Unit 2: Measurements and Scientific Methods

questions.question_text_en: One of the following is NOT a cause of uncertainty in measurement?

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: The person doing the experiment

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: The type of material measured

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: The environment where the measurement is made

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: The measuring device

explanation.solution_text_en:
Common measurement uncertainty arises from the measuring instrument, observer, and environment. The “type of 
material” itself is not normally listed as a source of measurement uncertainty.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 9 Chemistry — Unit 2: Measurements and Scientific Methods

questions.question_text_en:
Hydrogen bonding occurs in compounds that contain H-N, H-O and H-F bonds. These bonds are stronger than the ordinary 
dipole-dipole interactions because

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: the H-N, H-O and H-F bonds are less polar than ordinary covalent bonds

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: the partially positive H of one molecule is attracted to the partially negative lone pairs on the N, O or F of another molecule

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: the H-N, H-O and H-F bonds are non-polar and thus do not interact with neighboring molecules

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: the small sizes of N, O and F makes these atoms so electropositive that their covalently bonded H is highly negative

explanation.solution_text_en: Hydrogen bonding is the attraction between a δ⁺ H bonded to N/O/F and a lone pair on N/O/F of another molecule.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 11 Chemistry — Unit 2: Chemical Bonding

questions.question_text_en: Which of the following is an example of exception to the octet rule?

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: CCl₄

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: NH₃

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: PCl₅

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: H₂ O

explanation.solution_text_en: PCl₅ is an expanded-octet molecule: phosphorus has more than eight electrons around it in the Lewis description.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 11 Chemistry — Unit 2: Chemical Bonding

questions.question_text_en:
Which of the following pair is true about the general properties of the different types of crystalline solids Type of solid 
Hardness Melting point Conduction of heat and electricity I. Ionic Hard High Good II. Covalent Hard High Poor III. Molecular 
Soft Low Good IV. Metallic Soft to hard Low to high Good
questions.review_note:
The conductivity row for ionic solids is oversimplified; ionic substances conduct well when molten or aqueous, not 
as ordinary solids.

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: II and III

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: I and III

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: I and IV

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: I and II

explanation.solution_text_en:
The table is oversimplified because ionic solids conduct when molten or in solution, not well as solids. Under the 
intended classification, ionic and metallic entries are treated as the correct pair, option C.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 11 Chemistry — Unit 2: Chemical Bonding

questions.question_text_en:
When the boiling point of hydrides of group VIA elements, H₂ O, H₂ S, H₂ Se and H₂ Te are arranged in the order of 
increasing boiling point. The trend is H₂ Te< H₂ Se< H₂ S< H₂ O, water having the highest boiling point, this is due to

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: the basic different structures of each hydride

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: the small size of O compared to the other group VIA elements

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: hydrogen bonding present in H₂ O molecules

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: increasing boiling points with increasing molecular mass

explanation.solution_text_en:
H₂O has unusually strong intermolecular hydrogen bonding, raising its boiling point far above the trend expected from 
molar mass alone.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 11 Chemistry — Unit 2: Chemical Bonding

questions.question_text_en:
Given the following catalyzed reactions2SO₂ (s) + O₂ (g) → 2SO₃ (g); V₂ O₅ (s) as a catalystOCl (aq) + I⁻ (aq) → Ol⁻ (aq) + Cl 
(aq); OH⁻ (aq) as inhibitorCO (s) + H₂ (g) → CH₄ (g) + H₂ O (g); Ni (s) as a catalystCO (s) + H₂ (g) → HCHO (g); Cu (s) as a 
catalyst Which reaction(s) is/ are examples for homogeneous catalysis?

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: II only

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: I and II

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: IV only

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: II and III

explanation.solution_text_en:
A homogeneous catalyst or inhibitor is in the same phase as the reacting species. Reaction II has all relevant 
species in aqueous solution, whereas the solid catalysts in I, III and IV are heterogeneous.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 11 Chemistry — Unit 4: Chemical Kinetics

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following is a common reaction of tin?

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Sn (s) + H₂ O (g) → SnO₂ (s)

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Sn (s) + dil. 2HCl (aq) → SnCl₂ (aq) +H₂ (g)

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Sn (s) + 2Cl₂ (g) → SnCl₂ (s) in cold media

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Sn (s) + 2H₂ O (g) → Sn(OH)₄ (s)

explanation.solution_text_en: Tin reacts with dilute HCl to form SnCl₂ and H₂: Sn + 2HCl → SnCl₂ + H₂.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 10 Chemistry — Unit 5: Metals and Nonmetals

questions.question_text_en: The monomer of natural rubber is

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: 2-methyl-1,3-butadiene (isoprene)CH₂ =C(CH₃)-CH=CH₂

choices.label: B
choices.text_en:
2-chloro-1,3-butadiene (chloroprene)​
H2C=C(Cl)-CH=CH2

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Styrene (C₆H₅-CH=CH₂)

choices.label: D
choices.text_en:
1,3-butadiene​
H2C=CH-CH=CH2

explanation.solution_text_en: Natural rubber is polyisoprene, so its monomer is 2-methyl-1,3-butadiene (isoprene).
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 12 Chemistry — Unit 4: Polymers

questions.question_text_en: All of the following are examples of addition polymers EXCEPT
questions.review_note: No unambiguous EXCEPT option is preserved in the source.

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: -[CH₂ -CHCl] n -

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: -[CH₂ -CH₂ ] n -

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: -[CH₂ CH₂ ] n -[CH₂ -CH(CH₃)] n -

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Polystyrene -[CH₂-CH(C₆H₅)]ₙ-

explanation.solution_text_en:
The visible formulas correspond to addition polymers, including PVC, polyethylene/copolymer structures and 
polystyrene. No unambiguous “EXCEPT” choice remains in the source, so the item is defective.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 12 Chemistry — Unit 4: Polymers

questions.question_text_en: One of the following examples of polymers is correctly matched with its uses
questions.review_note: Non-unique item: both polyethylene food containers and PVC pipes are standard uses.

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Polypropylene; electrical insulation

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Polyethylene; food containers

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Polytetrafluoroethylene; making shoes

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Polyvinyl chloride; making pipes

explanation.solution_text_en:
Polyethylene is widely used for food containers, and PVC is widely used for pipes. Both B and D are chemically 
reasonable, making the item non-unique.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 12 Chemistry — Unit 4: Polymers

questions.question_text_en: Natural polymers are

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: polymers produced by condensation reaction of monomer units

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: polymers produced by the addition reaction of monomer units.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: polymers produced by the substitution of one or more atoms in the monomer units.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: polymers found in some substances like rubber in nature.

explanation.solution_text_en: Natural polymers are macromolecules occurring in nature, such as natural rubber, cellulose and proteins.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 12 Chemistry — Unit 4: Polymers

questions.question_text_en: Oils are unsaturated fatty acids. The process of converting oils to solid fats involves

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: saponification with NaOH.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: esterification of the acids.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: halogenations of the C-C double bonds.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: hydrogenation of the C-C double bonds.

explanation.solution_text_en:
Hydrogenation adds H₂ across C=C double bonds in unsaturated oils, increasing saturation and converting them 
toward more solid fats.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 12 Chemistry — Unit 4: Polymers

questions.question_text_en:
A chemistry teacher has added different reactants and reagents in three different test tubes as described below: I. Into the 
test tube A, he added ethanol, sodium dichromate, sulphuric acid. II. Into the test tube B, he added acetaldehyde, sodium 
borohydride and water. III. Into the tube C, he added methyl acetate and ethanol and sodium hydroxide.​
In which test tube would a reaction take place that provide acetic acid?

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: I and II

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: III

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: I

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: II and III

explanation.solution_text_en:
Acidified dichromate oxidizes ethanol through ethanal to ethanoic (acetic) acid. NaBH₄ reduces acetaldehyde, and 
base hydrolysis of methyl acetate gives acetate unless acidified.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 11 Chemistry — Unit 6: Some Important Oxygen-containing Organic Compounds

questions.question_text_en: The difference between colloids and suspension is that

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: most colloids and suspensions appear cloudy.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: colloidal particles are small enough and do not settle down unlike in a suspension.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: colloids are as transparent as solutions.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: both colloids and suspensions are heterogeneous mixtures.

explanation.solution_text_en:
Colloidal particles are small enough to remain dispersed and generally do not settle under gravity, unlike suspension 
particles.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 10 Chemistry — Unit 2: Solutions

questions.question_text_en: The solubility of a substance is the amount of a substance that

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: dissolves more amount of solute than it can normally dissolve.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: gives an unsaturated solution of substance at given temperature.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: dissolves double the amount of solute than it can normally dissolve.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: gives a saturated solution of the substance at a given temperature.

explanation.solution_text_en:
Solubility is the maximum amount of solute that forms a saturated solution under specified conditions, especially 
temperature.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 10 Chemistry — Unit 2: Solutions

questions.question_text_en:
50 mL of the supernatant saturated solution of NaCl was taken in an evaporating dish (weight=w₀) and evaporated over a 
Bunsen burner until all the water has evaporated and dry sodium chloride is left in the evaporating dish. The evaporating 
dish with the dry sodium chloride is weighed (weight=w₁). Given the following information, w₀=47.5 g and w₁=66.2. Calculate 
the solubility of NaCl in water assuming 50 mL of the solution is equal to 50 mL of the solvent

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: 113.7 g/100 g of water

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: 37.4 g/100 g of water

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: 187 g/100 g of water

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: 18.7g/100 g of water

explanation.solution_text_en:
Mass of NaCl = 66.2 − 47.5 = 18.7 g. Using the stated approximation of 50 g water, solubility = 18.7/50 ×100 = 37.4 g 
per 100 g water.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 10 Chemistry — Unit 2: Solutions

questions.question_text_en: One of the following given pairs represents examples of buffer systems

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: NH₄Cl/H₂O and H₂O/CH₃COONa

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: NaOH/HCl and HNO₃/KOH

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: NH₄OH/NH₄Cl and CH₃COOH/CH₃COONa

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: NH₄OH/CH₃COOH and NH₄Cl/CH₃COONa

explanation.solution_text_en:
A buffer contains a weak acid/base together with its conjugate salt. NH₄OH/NH₄Cl and CH₃COOH/CH₃COONa are 
standard buffer pairs.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 12 Chemistry — Unit 1: Acid-Base Concepts

questions.question_text_en:
The reaction between a weak acid and strong base as represented by the reaction between acetic acid and NaOH gives a 
basic solution because

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: CH₃OO⁻ as a strong base picks up H+ and causes excess OH⁻ ions.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Na+ is a strong acid and causes high concentration of H+.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: CH₃COOH does not produce sufficient amount of H+ ions.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: The OH⁻ ions from NaOH are not completely neutralized.

explanation.solution_text_en:
After neutralization of a weak acid by a strong base, acetate hydrolyzes water to produce OH⁻, so the solution is 
basic. Option A expresses this intended idea.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 12 Chemistry — Unit 1: Acid-Base Concepts

questions.question_text_en: An acid is a substance that

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: produces more OH ions in water than H+ ions.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: has a bitter taste.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: donates a pair of electrons to a chemical species.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: donates a proton in a chemical reaction.

explanation.solution_text_en: In Brønsted–Lowry theory, an acid is a proton donor.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 12 Chemistry — Unit 1: Acid-Base Concepts

questions.question_text_en: One of the following given mass of acids constitutes the corresponding equivalent of the acid

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: HCl = 36.5 g=2 equivalents

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: H₂SO₄=98 g=2 equivalent

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: H₃PO₄= 98 g=2 equivalents

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: H₂SO₄= 49 g= 4 equivalents

explanation.solution_text_en: One mole (98 g) of H₂SO₄ can supply two moles of H⁺, so 98 g corresponds to two acid equivalents.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 12 Chemistry — Unit 1: Acid-Base Concepts

questions.question_text_en: One of the following pairs shows Brønsted-Lowry acids behavior in water?

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: H₃ O⁺ and NH₃

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: HNO₃ and NO₃⁻

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: HCl and NH₄⁺

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: HPO₄²⁻ and PO₄³⁻

explanation.solution_text_en: HCl and NH₄⁺ can each donate a proton to water, so both behave as Brønsted–Lowry acids.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 12 Chemistry — Unit 1: Acid-Base Concepts

questions.question_text_en:
Covalent compounds are liquids or gases at room temperature and have statements low melting and boiling points. Which of 
the following statements explains these properties of covalent compounds?

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: The unit of particles in covalent compounds are ions.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: The intermolecular forces of attraction in covalent compounds are strong.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Covalent compounds exist as separate molecules.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: There are no forces of attraction between the molecules in covalent compounds.

explanation.solution_text_en:
Many molecular covalent substances have low melting/boiling points because the molecules are held together by 
relatively weak intermolecular forces; option C is the closest statement.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 11 Chemistry — Unit 2: Chemical Bonding

questions.question_text_en:
Both carbonyl sulphide, COS (SCO), S=C=O and carbon dioxide (CO₂) O=C=O are linear molecules. COS is polar whereas 
CO₂ is non-polar. This is because

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: the C=O bonds in both COS and CO2 are polar.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: CO2 has a net dipole moment of zero.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: sulphur is more electronegative than oxygen.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: regions of high negative charge is distributed equally around the central atom in COS.

explanation.solution_text_en:
Linear CO₂ has two equal C=O bond dipoles that cancel, giving zero net dipole moment. COS has different terminal 
atoms, so its bond dipoles do not cancel.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 11 Chemistry — Unit 2: Chemical Bonding

questions.question_text_en: Which of the following statements is true about the formation of CH4 according to valence bond theory?

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: The 2s and three 2p orbitals in carbon hybridize to form four sp³ orbitals.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: The 2s and two 2p orbitals in carbon hybridize to form three sp² orbitals.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Carbon can form two hybrid orbitals as it has got only two half-filled orbitals.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: The 2s and one 2p orbitals in carbon hybridize to form two sp orbitals.

explanation.solution_text_en: Methane is described by four equivalent sp³ hybrid orbitals formed from one 2s and three 2p orbitals on carbon.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 11 Chemistry — Unit 2: Chemical Bonding

questions.question_text_en:
Phosphorus (Z=15) has the electronic configuration 1s²2s²2p⁶3s²3p³, what kind of hybridization does phosphorus undergo in 
the formation of phosphorus pentachloride (PCl5)?

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: sp³d

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: sp³

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: sp

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: sp²

explanation.solution_text_en:
PCl₅ has five electron domains around P and is described by sp³d hybridization in the conventional valence-bond 
model used at this level.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 11 Chemistry — Unit 2: Chemical Bonding

questions.question_text_en: One of the following reactions illustrates the formation of coordinate covalent bond?

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Be + 2F2 → BeF2

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: NaOH + HCl → NaCl+H2O

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: CaCO3+ HCl → CaCl2 +H2O +CO2

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: NH3 + HCl → NH4+ + Cl-

explanation.solution_text_en: NH₃ donates its lone pair to H⁺ from HCl, forming NH₄⁺; that new N–H bond is a coordinate covalent bond.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 11 Chemistry — Unit 2: Chemical Bonding

questions.question_text_en:
In the production of NH3 by the Haber process according to the equation​
N2(g)+3H2(g) ⇌ 2NH3(g) ΔH=-92KJ mol-1​
What are the favorable conditions for the production of high yield of NH3?

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: High pressure and low temperature

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Low pressure and low temperature

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Low pressure and high temperature

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: High pressure and high temperature

explanation.solution_text_en:
The Haber equilibrium is exothermic and decreases gas moles from 4 to 2. High pressure and lower temperature 
favor NH₃ yield, although industry uses a compromise temperature for rate.
explanation.key_concept:
Curriculum link: Grade 11 Chemistry — Unit 5: Chemical Equilibrium (Haber equilibrium) 
ESSLCE Chemistry 2013 E.C. | Questions, Answers & Explanations

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following statements describes laboratory and industrial preparation of acetic respectively?

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Reduction of ethanol by NaBH4 and fermentation of propanol.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Reduction of toluene by KMnO4 and reduction of ethanol by sodium dichromate.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: The oxidation of ethanol by sodium dichromate and fermentation of ethanol.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Oxidation of toluene by KMnO4 and fermentation of ethanol.

explanation.solution_text_en:
Ethanoic acid can be prepared in the laboratory by oxidizing ethanol; industrial/biochemical production can involve 
oxidation/fermentation of ethanol. Option C is the intended pair.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 11 Chemistry — Unit 6: Some Important Oxygen-containing Organic Compounds

questions.question_text_en: Which of the following is true about carboxylic acids?

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Methanoic, Ethanoic and Citric acids are monocarboxylic acids.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Carboxylic acid with the formation RCOOH.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Citric acid is a typical dicarboxylic acid.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Propanedioic acid is the simplest dicarboxylic acid.

explanation.solution_text_en: The functional group of a monocarboxylic acid is RCOOH, which is the general structural description in option B.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 11 Chemistry — Unit 6: Some Important Oxygen-containing Organic Compounds

questions.question_text_en: What is the IUPAC name for the branched carboxylic acid: CH₃ -CH(Cl)-CH(CH₃)-CH(CH₃)-COOH

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: 4-chloro-2, methyl 1-pentanoic acid

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: 1, 2-dimethyl-4-chloro 1-pentanoic acid

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: 4-chloro-1-methyl-1-pentanoic acid

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: 4-chloro-2, 3-dimethyl-1-pentanoic acid

explanation.solution_text_en: Numbering from the carboxyl carbon gives 4-chloro-2,3-dimethylpentanoic acid, corresponding to D.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 11 Chemistry — Unit 6: Some Important Oxygen-containing Organic Compounds

questions.question_text_en: Esters are characterized by the following properties EXCEPT
questions.review_note: The intended answer is C, but option D is also an overgeneralized/false statement as written.

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: esters have lower boiling point compared to the carboxylic acid alcohols

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: esters have pleasant odors of perfumes and food flavoring

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: esters have higher boiling point than carboxylic acid and alcohol

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: all esters are soluble in inorganic solvents and organic

explanation.solution_text_en:
Esters generally have lower boiling points than comparable carboxylic acids/alcohols and many have pleasant odors. 
The intended EXCEPT is C; note that D is also overgeneralized because not all esters are soluble in all solvents.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 11 Chemistry — Unit 6: Some Important Oxygen-containing Organic Compounds

questions.question_text_en:
The sanitizer in wide use for protection against Covid-19 is labelled 83% alcohol. How can one scientifically check the 
concentration?

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: experimentation

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: forming hypothesis

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: making observation

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: collection of data

explanation.solution_text_en: A labeled concentration is scientifically checked by measurement/experiment, not by hypothesis alone.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 9 Chemistry — Unit 2: Measurements and Scientific Methods

questions.question_text_en: The correct electronic configuration for chromium (Cr, Z=24) is

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: 1s²2s²2p⁶3s²3p⁶4s⁰3d⁶

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: 1s²2s²2p⁶3s²3p⁶3d⁴4d²

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: 1s²2s²2p⁶3s²3p⁶4s²3d⁴

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: 1s²2s²2p⁶3s²3p⁶4s¹3d⁵

explanation.solution_text_en: Chromium has the exceptional ground-state configuration [Ar] 3d⁵4s¹, giving a particularly stable half-filled d subshell.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 11 Chemistry — Unit 1: Atomic Structure and Periodic Properties of the Elements

questions.question_text_en: According to Hund's rule equal energy (degenerate) orbitals are filled with

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: maximum number of unpaired electrons with parallel spins

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: two electrons of opposite spins placed in the first orbitals

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: maximum number of unpaired electrons with opposite spins

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: two electrons of parallel spins placed in the first orbital

explanation.solution_text_en: Hund’s rule fills degenerate orbitals singly with parallel spins before electron pairing begins.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 11 Chemistry — Unit 1: Atomic Structure and Periodic Properties of the Elements

questions.question_text_en: In the modern periodic table

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: elements with similar properties are placed in the same period

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: non-metals are placed on the right side of the periodic table

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: transition and inner-transition elements are placed in the middle of the periodic table

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: metals are placed on the right hand side of the periodic table

explanation.solution_text_en:
Nonmetals are primarily on the right side of the modern periodic table; similar chemical properties occur mainly within 
groups, not periods.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 11 Chemistry — Unit 1: Atomic Structure and Periodic Properties of the Elements

questions.question_text_en:
The electrolysis of liquid (molten) NaCl in the set-up for the electrochemical cell is given in the following figure below. Which 
of the following statements is true about the electrolysis of molten sodium chloride? 
[Source image unavailable/corrupted in archive]

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Na is oxidized at the anode

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Cl₂ is formed at the cathode

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: O₂ is produced at the anode due to the oxidation of water

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: The net reaction produces Cl₂ at the anode and Na at the cathode.

explanation.solution_text_en: Molten NaCl contains only Na⁺ and Cl⁻: Na⁺ is reduced to Na at the cathode, while Cl⁻ is oxidized to Cl₂ at the anode.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 12 Chemistry — Unit 2: Electrochemistry

questions.question_text_en: In the reaction mixture of two species NH₄ OH and NH₄ Cl, which one of the following is true about the reaction mixture?

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: The presence of NH₄⁺ ion suppresses the dissociation of the weak based NH₄ OH.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: The NH₄⁺ ion is a spectator ion in the reaction mixture.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: The reaction equilibrium is shifted towards the right due to the presence of NH₄⁺ ions.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: The presence of NH₄⁺ in the reaction mixture makes the solution more basic.

explanation.solution_text_en:
Adding NH₄⁺ from NH₄Cl shifts NH₄OH/NH₃ ionization toward the un-ionized weak base, illustrating the common-ion 
effect.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 12 Chemistry — Unit 1: Acid-Base Concepts

questions.question_text_en:
Which one of the following is correct about K w at different temperature? The ionic product of water K w equals K w 
=1.0x10⁻¹⁴ at 25 °C K w =2.92x10⁻¹⁴ at 40 °C √K w =1x10⁻⁷ √K w =1x10⁻⁷

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: At 40 ^o C pure water is no more neutral

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Water dissociates to a higher extent at 40 ^o C than at 25 ^o C.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Hydroxyl ion concentration is higher at 40 ^o than hydrogen ion concentration

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Hydrogen ion concentration at 25 ^o C is higher than at 40 ^o C.

explanation.solution_text_en:
Because Kw increases with temperature in the data given, water autoionizes to a greater extent at 40°C. Pure water 
is still neutral because [H⁺] = [OH⁻].
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 12 Chemistry — Unit 1: Acid-Base Concepts

questions.question_text_en: What is reduction? Reduction is

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: loss of electrons and decrease in oxidation number

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: gain of electrons and increase in oxidation number

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: gain of electrons and no change in oxidation number

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: gain of electrons and decrease in oxidation number

explanation.solution_text_en: Reduction is gain of electrons and therefore a decrease in oxidation number.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 12 Chemistry — Unit 2: Electrochemistry

questions.question_text_en:
During the electrolysis of dilute aqueous sulphuric acid, the ions present in solution are H⁺, OH⁻ and SO₄²⁻. Which ions are 
preferentially discharged at the cathode and anode, respectively?

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Anode = SO₄²⁻ (aq) + 4H⁺ (aq) +2e⁻ → SO₂ (g) + 2H₂ O, Cathode=2H⁺ (aq) + 2e⁻ → H₂ (g)

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Anode=4OH(aq) → H₂ O(l) + O₂ (g) +4e⁻, Cathode=2H⁺ (aq) +2e⁻ → H₂ (g)

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Anode= 2H₂ O(l) → O₂ (g) + 4H⁺ (aq) +4e⁻, Cathode=2H⁺ (aq) +2e⁻ → H₂ (g)

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Anode=4OH(aq) → H₂ O(l) + O₂ (g) +4e⁻, Cathode=2H₂ O (l) +2e⁻ → H₂ (g) + 2OH⁻ (aq)

explanation.solution_text_en:
In dilute sulfuric acid, H⁺ is reduced to H₂ at the cathode and water is oxidized to O₂ at the anode. Option C gives the 
appropriate acidic half-reactions.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 12 Chemistry — Unit 2: Electrochemistry

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following is NOT correct about electrodes and electrochemical cells?

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: The overall cell potential is calculated by the formula E° cell =E Cathode − E Anode

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Electrons flow spontaneously from negative to positive electrodes

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: The difference in the electrical potential of the electrode is positive that is positive cell

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: E° cell is greater than zero for non-spontaneous process

explanation.solution_text_en:
For a spontaneous galvanic cell E°cell must be positive. Therefore the statement that E°cell > 0 for a 
non-spontaneous process is false.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 12 Chemistry — Unit 2: Electrochemistry

questions.question_text_en: The "like dissolves like" rule accounts for one of the following observation
questions.review_note: Non-unique item: B and C both follow the polarity principle “like dissolves like.”

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: The solubility of C₂ H₆ in H₂ O.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: The solubility of C₆ H₆ in CCl₄.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: The insolubility of I₂ in H₂ O.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: The solubility of KBr in C₇ H₈.

explanation.solution_text_en:
“Like dissolves like” predicts nonpolar benzene dissolves in nonpolar CCl₄, and it also explains why nonpolar I₂ is 
poorly soluble in polar water. The item therefore admits B and C as consistent observations.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 10 Chemistry — Unit 2: Solutions

questions.question_text_en: Which of the following concentration units is correctly defined?
questions.review_note: Source formulas are incomplete/corrupted; no listed definition is fully correct.

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: ppm (parts per million) = (mass of solute/ mass of solvent) x 10⁶

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: mass percentage= mass of solute x 100

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: mass percentage= mass of solute x 100

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: ppb (parts per billion)= (mass of solute/mass of solution) x 10⁶

explanation.solution_text_en:
The standard definitions are mass % = (mass solute/mass solution)×100, ppm ≈ (mass solute/mass solution)×10⁶, 
and ppb ≈ ×10⁹. The supplied formulas are incomplete/incorrect, so no option is fully valid.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 10 Chemistry — Unit 2: Solutions

questions.question_text_en:
The concentrated sulphuric acid H₂ SO₄ we use in the laboratory is 98% H₂ SO₄ by mass and has a density of 1.83 g/mL. 
Below are given the concentrations of the acid in various units, which of the given alternatives correctly describes the 
concentration of the acid?

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Molarity 36.6 M, Normality 18.3 N, Mole fraction 0.1

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Molarity 18.3 M, Normality 36.6 N, Mole fraction 0.9

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Molarity 1.83 M, Normality 3.66 N, Mole fraction 0.9

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Molarity 18.3 M, Normality 3.66 N, Mole fraction 0.9

explanation.solution_text_en:
In 1.00 L, solution mass is 1830 g and H₂SO₄ mass is 1793.4 g, about 18.3 mol. Thus molarity ≈18.3 M, normality 
≈36.6 N for a diprotic acid, and mole fraction is about 0.9.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 10 Chemistry — Unit 2: Solutions

questions.question_text_en: How do you prepare 500mL of 1N Ca(OH)₂ solution?
questions.review_note: Correct preparation requires 18.5 g Ca(OH)₂ in 500 mL; no option states this.

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: By dissolving 74 g of Ca(OH)₂ in 500 mL of solution.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: By dissolving 37 g of Ca(OH)₂ in 1 liter of solution.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: By dissolving 37 g of Ca(OH)₂ in 500 mL of solution.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: By dissolving 74 g of Ca(OH)₂ in 1 liter of solution.

explanation.solution_text_en:
Ca(OH)₂ has equivalent mass 74/2 = 37 g per equivalent. A 1 N, 0.500 L solution needs 18.5 g, which is absent from 
the options.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 10 Chemistry — Unit 2: Solutions

questions.question_text_en: The K a of acetic acid CH₃ COOH is 1.8 x 10⁻⁵. What is the percent ionization of 1M of CH₃ COOH?
questions.review_note: Calculated percent ionization is about 0.424%; no listed option matches.

explanation.solution_text_en:
For 1.0 M CH₃COOH with Ka = 1.8×10⁻⁵, [H⁺] ≈ √KaC = 4.24×10⁻³ M, giving about 0.424% ionization. None of the 
listed percentages matches.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 10 Chemistry — Unit 2: Solutions

questions.question_text_en: The mathematical expressions for Faraday's first law is summarized as

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: m= ^Mt / nF

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: n= ^mlt / MF

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: m= ^mt / F

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: M= ^mlt / nF

explanation.solution_text_en:
Faraday’s law gives m = MIt/(nF), where M is molar mass, I current, t time, n electrons per ion, and F Faraday 
constant.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 12 Chemistry — Unit 2: Electrochemistry

questions.question_text_en:
In the electrolysis of copper sulphate solution using graphite electrodes, O₂ is liberated at the anode and copper metal is 
deposited at the cathode. If the electrolysis of CuSO₄ is performed using copper electrode, what happens at the anode and 
cathode?

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: At the anode H₂ is liberated, whereas copper is deposited at the cathode.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: At the anode the copper electrode dissolves and copper metal is deposited at the cathode.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: No electrochemical reaction takes place involving copper.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: At the anode copper is reduced, whereas copper is oxidized at the cathode.

explanation.solution_text_en: With copper electrodes, the anode dissolves: Cu → Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻, while Cu²⁺ is reduced and plated at the cathode.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 12 Chemistry — Unit 2: Electrochemistry

questions.question_text_en:
The statement 'the amount of a substance consumed or of produced in an electrolytic cell is directly proportional to the 
amount of electricity that passes through the cell' is known as

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Raoult's law.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Dalton's law.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Henry's law.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Faraday's law.

explanation.solution_text_en: That proportionality between amount electrolyzed and electric charge is Faraday’s first law of electrolysis.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 12 Chemistry — Unit 2: Electrochemistry

questions.question_text_en:
Given the standard reduction potentials: Cu +0.34 V, Pb −0.13 V, Ni −0.25 V, Cd −0.40 V, Zn −0.76 V, Al −1.66 V, Ca −2.87 
V, K −2.93 V. Which statement is correct about the reactivity of the metals?

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: K is the strongest reducing agent among the listed metals.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Cu is the strongest reducing agent in the group.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Pb is more easily oxidized than Al.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: The reaction Cu + Zn²⁺ ⇌ Cu²⁺ + Zn is spontaneous.

explanation.solution_text_en:
A more negative standard reduction potential corresponds to a metal that is more readily oxidized and therefore a 
stronger reducing agent. K is strongest among the listed metals.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 12 Chemistry — Unit 2: Electrochemistry

questions.question_text_en: One of the following is NOT true about the effects of corrosion?

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: It causes enormous damage to buildings, bridges, ships and cars.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: It causes deterioration of metals by spontaneous chemical process.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Corrosion forms protection oxide layers to prevent damage.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Damage from corrosion costs billions of dollars annually.

explanation.solution_text_en:
Corrosion is damaging oxidation of metals. Although some oxide films can be protective (passivation), that is not an 
“effect of corrosion” in the intended damaging sense.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 12 Chemistry — Unit 2: Electrochemistry

questions.question_text_en: Which statement is true about catalysts?

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: A positive catalyst decreases the rate of a reaction by increasing the activation energy.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: A catalyst slows down or speeds up a reaction, itself being consumed.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: The role of a catalyst is to increase or decrease the rate of a reaction by lowering or increasing the activation energy.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: A negative catalyst increases the rate of a reaction by decreasing the value of activation energy.

explanation.solution_text_en:
Catalysts modify reaction rate by providing an alternative pathway with different activation energy. The wording in C 
best captures the intended distinction between positive and negative catalysts.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 11 Chemistry — Unit 4: Chemical Kinetics

questions.question_text_en: According to the transition state theory

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: in the activated complex, the original bonds are weakened and the new bonds are partially formed.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en:
the collision between two reacting species results in the formation of an activated complex, which has less energy than both 
the reactants and products.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: the standard reaction enthalpy (ΔH°) depends on the magnitude of the activation energy (Ea).

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: the activation energy is the energy that must be absorbed or released by reactants to reach the activated complex.

explanation.solution_text_en:
At the transition state, old bonds are partly broken and new bonds are partly formed; this high-energy arrangement is 
the activated complex.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 11 Chemistry — Unit 4: Chemical Kinetics

questions.question_text_en: Which of the following is true about the rate reactant?

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: The value of a rate constant tells us how fast or slow a reaction is.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: It expresses the relationship between the rate of a chemical reaction and the volume of reacting species.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: A small rate constant indicates a faster reaction and a larger rate indicates a slower reaction.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: The value of a rate constant is independent of reaction conditions.

explanation.solution_text_en:
For a specified reaction and temperature, the magnitude of the rate constant k indicates how fast the reaction 
proceeds.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 11 Chemistry — Unit 4: Chemical Kinetics

questions.question_text_en:
For a first order reaction, the concentration versus time of the reaction mixture is given by the following graph If a is the initial 
concentration of the reactant and if the half-life is the 1hr, after how many hours would be the concentration of reactant 
produced to a/32?

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: 4hr

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: 1hr

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: 3hr

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: 5hr

explanation.solution_text_en: a/32 = a/(2⁵), so five half-lives are required. At 1 hour per half-life, the time is 5 hours.

questions.question_text_en:
The mathematical expression log k=(-E a /2.303R)1/T + log A derived from the Arrhenius equation is of important as it 
shows

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: for a given value of activation energy the value of the rate constant increases as the temperature increases.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: reactions with larger activation energies have higher values of k and are therefore faster.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: for a given value of activation energy, the value of the rate constant decreases as the temperature increases.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: reactions with larger activation energies, the value of the rate constant decreases as the temperature increases.

explanation.solution_text_en: Arrhenius behavior shows that, for fixed activation energy, k increases as temperature increases.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 11 Chemistry — Unit 4: Chemical Kinetics

questions.question_text_en: Which of the following is true about isotopes? Isotopes of an element have

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: different number of neutrons and same number of protons.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: the same number of electrons and neutrons.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: the same atomic mass but different atomic numbers.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: different physical and chemical properties.

explanation.solution_text_en: Isotopes have the same proton number (same element) but different neutron numbers, so their mass numbers differ.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 11 Chemistry — Unit 1: Atomic Structure and Periodic Properties of the Elements

questions.question_text_en: Which statement correctly describes Heisenberg's uncertainty principle?

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: A particle with a mass moving at a given speed can be described by the wave characteristic of material particles.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: If we measure the momentum of a particle precisely then its position will be correspondingly precise.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Both the location and the momentum of a subatomic particle like the electron cannot be precisely known.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: A small particle like the reaction can behave both as a particle and a wave.

explanation.solution_text_en:
Heisenberg’s uncertainty principle states that position and momentum cannot both be known with arbitrary precision 
at the same time.

questions.question_text_en: Which of the following statements is correct about energy changes when an electron changes its energy level?
questions.review_note:
Non-unique item: A and D are both correct descriptions for downward and upward electronic transitions, 
respectively.

choices.label: A
choices.text_en:
When an electron falls from a higher energy level to a lower energy level, energy equal to the difference between the two 
energy levels is emitted.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en:
When an electron jumps from a lower energy level to a higher level, a photon is emitted with energy equal to the difference 
between the two energy levels.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en:
When an electron falls from a higher energy level to a lower energy level, the energy emitted is greater than the difference 
between the two energy levels.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en:
When an electron jumps from a lower energy level to a higher energy level, energy equal to the difference between the two 
energy levels is absorbed.

explanation.solution_text_en:
For an upward transition, the atom absorbs ΔE; for a downward transition, it emits ΔE. Thus A and D state the two 
complementary correct cases, making the item non-unique.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 11 Chemistry — Unit 1: Atomic Structure and Periodic Properties of the Elements

questions.question_text_en: According to the Lewis definition of an acid, an acid is a substance that

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: accepts a H+ ion.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: dissociates in water to yield H3O+.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: accepts a pair of electrons.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: donates an OH- ion.

explanation.solution_text_en: A Lewis acid accepts an electron pair.

questions.question_text_en: Water is a weak electrolyte because

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: it can accept a proton from an acid and donate a proton to a base.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: it has a very high ionic product, Kw.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: it acts both as Bronsted-Lowry and base.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: it undergoes a reversible dissociation with a very low ionic product, Kw.

explanation.solution_text_en:
Pure water ionizes only very slightly and reversibly, so the concentration of ions is extremely small and water is a 
weak electrolyte.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 12 Chemistry — Unit 1: Acid-Base Concepts

questions.question_text_en: Which of the following reactions represent the amphiprotic behavior of water?

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: HCl + H₂O ⇌ H₃O⁺ + Cl⁻ and NH₃ + H₂O ⇌ NH₄⁺ + OH⁻

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: HCl + H₂O → H⁺ + Cl⁻ and NaOH + H₂O → Na⁺ + OH⁻

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: H₂O + H⁺ ⇌ H₃O⁺ and NH₃ + H⁺ ⇌ NH₄⁺

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: H₃O⁺ + OH⁻ → 2H₂O and H⁺ + OH⁻ → H₂O

explanation.solution_text_en:
In the HCl reaction water accepts H⁺ (acts as a base); in the NH₃ reaction water donates H⁺ (acts as an acid). 
Together these show amphiprotic behavior.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 12 Chemistry — Unit 1: Acid-Base Concepts

questions.question_text_en: For an acidic solution, which of the following is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: pH > pOH and pKw − pH < 7

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: pH = pOH and pH = ½pKw = 7

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: pH < 7 and [H⁺] < 1 × 10⁻⁷ M

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: pH < pOH and pKw − pH > 7

explanation.solution_text_en: At 25°C an acidic solution has pH < 7, pOH > 7, and therefore pH < pOH. Since pOH = pKw − pH, D is correct.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 12 Chemistry — Unit 1: Acid-Base Concepts

questions.question_text_en: What is the pH of 0.25 M HF solution at 25°C? HF(aq) + H₂O(l) ⇌ H₃O⁺(aq) + F⁻(aq), Kₐ = 6.8 × 10⁻⁴.

explanation.solution_text_en: For HF, Ka = x²/(0.25−x). Solving gives x ≈ 0.0127 M H₃O⁺ and pH ≈ 1.90, so 1.89 is the closest option.
